newsitem.title: UK: Analysts focus on ICI longer-term outlook.
newsitem.headline: Analysts focus on ICI longer-term outlook.

text.p: Shares in British chemicals giant Imperial Chemical Industries Plc were boosted on Tuesday after the European Commission waved through its purchase of Unilever Plc's speciality chemical arm.
Although analysts said the green light had been expected, it helped shake the shares out of a recent sharp decline which was sparked by a round of earnings downgrades from major brokerages.

After tumbling 41 pence on Monday as word of the sharp reductions to profit forecasts spread round the market, ICI fell a further 14-1/2 pence at one stage on Tuesday before recovering to be up 4-1/2p at 813 by 1415 GMT.

Some ICI watchers said investors should focus on the company's longer-term prospects, underlined by the Unilever move and the planned disposal of its bulk chemical operations, rather than on any short-term pressure on its profitability.

They pointed out that the stock was probably due a correction after a 23 percent rise since early May -- yet in the longer term, a different ICI was about to emerge from the battered hulk of the old, they said.
"The results over the next two years will be irrelevant (to ICI's long-term appeal)," said Peter Blair, analyst at Salomon Brothers.
"It is a longer-term transition story, the commodity chemicals are going to be sold off and with ICI you have to focus on the longer-term prospects."

Nodding through ICI's acquisition of Unilever's National Starch, Unichema and Crosfield units seven weeks after it was first proposed, the European Commission said it did not give rise to competition concerns.

Although Williams de Broe analyst Peter Cartwright said he had scaled back his 1997 pre-tax profit forecast to between 450 million pounds and 500 million pounds, he said the shares would be a "buy" not far below current levels.
"Next year will be a year of transition and by 1999 we will be looking at a new company," Cartwright said.
Monday's earnings reductions came after ICI held its traditional round of analyst briefings in the run-up to its first-half results due at the end of next month.

Warning over the impact of continuing sterling strength and weak bulk chemical prices, Merrill analysts cut their current-year profit forecasts to 450 million stg from 530 million and their 1998 forecasts to 640 million stg from 740 million.
Dresdner Kleinwort Benson cut by a similar degree, to 440 million stg from 540 million for 1997. It repeated a "sell" rating on the shares.

Yet Blair at Salomon played down the significance of the latest downgrades, saying forecasts at the top end of the range had looked vulnerable and that he had lowered his numbers -- to 446 million stg for 1997 and to 536 million for 1997 -- some weeks ago.
Blair said there were signs that U.S. investors, seen underpinning the strength in ICI shares since early May, were happier to took at ICI's prospects beyond the next two years.
"Americans like the transformation story," he said, "and they may be taking a longer-term view."
